title: LethAL explain output
description: What `lethal explain <report.json>` prints on stdout. THE SPLIT CONTRACT, which the payload also states in its own `contract` block: STRUCTURE is contractual and versioned by explainSchemaVersion; PROSE is not, and may improve without a bump. Every machine-usable fact is a field, so no consumer has a reason to parse a `meaning` string. Additive fields do not bump the version, so tolerate properties you do not know.

explainSchemaVersion.description: The version of THIS document's structure.

derivedFromReportSchemaVersion.description: The report schemaVersion this projection was derived from. Recorded so the output stays self-describing once written to a file.

proseIsContractual.description: Branch on this rather than reading `note`.

score.description: The score with the qualifications that decide whether it may be quoted at all. Read `reliability` and `scoreDescribes` before quoting `mutationScore`.

mutationScore.description: Null when nothing was scored. Denominator is killed + timeoutKilled + survived.

scoreDescribes.description: The report's own sentence about what the number covers, verbatim.

excludedFromScore.description: Outcomes the number does NOT describe. Adding these to the survivors would double-count; ignoring them overstates what the run measured.

caveats.description: What bounds this run's result. Each arrives with the shared interpretation constant keyed to it.

survivorSelection.description: What `survivors` is a view OF. Always present, including when nothing was capped, so completeness is read rather than inferred from a missing field. Read `total` before treating `survivors` as the whole set.

total.description: Survivors in the report, before any cap.

omitted.description: total - shown. Zero when nothing was capped.

rankedBy.description: `report-order`: every survivor, in the order the report recorded them. `actionability`: the list was ranked by how much evidence each row carries and may be a prefix of it.

survivors.description: Mutants no test killed. A survivor is a LEAD, not a proven test-suite gap: check `executionProven` first.

originalText.description: The AL this operator replaced. A report from a real project carries that project's source here.

mutatedText.description: What it was replaced with. Empty string for a deletion operator, which is a fact rather than a missing value.

attribution.description: R252: `not-measured` appears only when the report's coverageMode is "none": no coverage was collected, so the survivor is neither covered nor uncovered.

executionProven.description: True ONLY for `exact`, a member-level coverage match: a test is measured to have executed the mutated procedure. False means some test touched the object and nothing proves the mutated code ran.

reach.description: Whether the mutated statement was reached. GH-24: the mutant's own guardReached decides first; a row carrying reachGrain without it is not-decided. Only a report without reachGrain falls back to what attribution and guardEvidence say TOGETHER.

reachGrain.description: GH-24: verbatim from the report row, the grain of the mutant's reach marker. Only `statement` has one. Absent for a report written before GH-24.

reachedBy.description: GH-24: the covering tests whose run reached the mutant's own statement. Present exactly when the report row has guardReached, so [] means none reached.

batchIndex.description: The batch of THIS run the row was recorded in. Mutant ids restart per batch, so (batchIndex, mutantCode) names a row and mutantCode alone does not. Always written by this build; optional here so an older explain output still validates.

triggerName.description: Present on a trigger mutant, whose procedureName is "".

coverageArmNames.description: R351: verbatim from the report row, the arm names of a renamed split member (R318), whose procedureName is "". Absent on every other member.

procedureStartLine.description: Verbatim from the report row: the 1-based first line of the enclosing procedure or trigger. Absent when neither encloses the site, or on a report predating this field.

procedureEndLine.description: Verbatim from the report row: the 1-based last line of the enclosing procedure or trigger.

equivalenceRisk.description: The equivalence risk this row's operator declared, on a survived row only. An open string. Absent means not recorded, never "not equivalent".

readerMark.description: The reader's mark whose key equals this row's identity, on a survived or known-survivor row. Absent means no mark matched, never that nobody looked.

artifactId.description: Verbatim from the report's artifacts[] entry whose batchIndex equals this row's: the artifact THIS run recorded for the row's batch. Not proof the verdict came from that binary. Absent exactly when artifactIdAbsent is present.

artifactIdAbsent.description: Why artifactId is absent. carried: the verdict was carried by --resume and measured against a prior run's artifact, which this report does not name. not-recorded: the report has no artifacts field (written before it existed). not-published: the report has artifacts but no entry for this batch.

gapId.description: C02-09: verbatim from the report row, the gap this survivor belongs to. Absent on a row from a report written before C02-09.

markKey.description: R265: the key a lethal.equivalent.json mark on this survivor needs, made by the same function the mark join matches against. Valid under markIdentityScheme.

notMeasured.description: Mutants recorded with an `error` verdict: excluded from the score, and NOT a verdict about the mutant. Never capped by --top.

cause.description: Present only when the report recorded a structural cause. Absent means the row's only account is `failureNote`.

gaps.description: C02-09: survivors grouped by gap block, one entry per gap id with at least one survived row. Present exactly when the report's rows carry gap ids, [] when none survived; absent on an older report. Never capped by --top.

gapId.description: G followed by 12 lowercase hex characters.

blockStartLine.description: 1-based first line of the gap block, the innermost branch body holding the mutants.

blockEndLine.description: 1-based last line of the gap block.

triggerName.description: Present on a trigger block, whose procedureName is "".

coverageArmNames.description: R351: verbatim from the report row, the arm names of a renamed split member (R318), whose procedureName is "". Absent on every other member.

members.description: mutantCodes of the gap's survived rows, ordered by line then mutantCode.

unobservedBlock.description: Every RECORDED row of the block survived. Absent on an operator- or line-narrowed run, which can drop mutants inside a block, and on a quarantined run, which stops scheduling mutants mid-run.

artifactId.description: The artifact to pass to lethal verify --artifact for this gap. Exactly one of this and artifactIdAbsent is present.

artifactIdAbsent.description: Why there is no artifact to verify this gap against. Same values as on a survivor; carried when any member is carried.

noCoverageBlocks.description: C02-09: blocks with at least one no-coverage row. A location list, not a verify input: no gap id, no counts. Present exactly when gaps is.

blockStartLine.description: 1-based first line of the gap block, the innermost branch body holding the mutants.

blockEndLine.description: 1-based last line of the gap block.

triggerName.description: Present on a trigger block, whose procedureName is "".

coverageArmNames.description: R351: verbatim from the report row, the arm names of a renamed split member (R318), whose procedureName is "". Absent on every other member.

members.description: mutantCodes of the block's no-coverage rows, ordered by line then mutantCode.

toolConditions.description: Conditions about LethAL's OWN state, as opposed to the target's code. This is the half the projection is fully prescriptive about.

count.description: How many mutants the condition accounts for. Always 0 for `quarantined`, whose cost was never scheduled and so cannot be counted.

markIdentityScheme.description: R265: the identityScheme a marks file needs for survivors[].markKey. The report's own identityScheme, and 1 when the report has none (R325).

markKeysStale.description: R265: present exactly when markIdentityScheme is not this build's identity scheme. A mark written from these keys would be stale on the next run under this build, so re-run first.

interpretation.description: What a machine value MEANS, plus a pointer at the evidence. Emitted by reference to a shared constant co-located with the value it is keyed to; never composed per call.

entailedNegative.description: What this rules OUT, when that is worth stating. Absent when there is no useful negative.

basis.description: A roadmap id such as `R29`, or a file such as `docs/measurements/README.md`. Never a bare claim.
